title: Protocol for live-cell fluorescence-guided cryoFIB-milling and electron cryo-tomography of virus-infected cells
protocol: Take a microscope slide and wrap it with parafilm.
Touch each grid in two locations away from the middle, with a sharp needle before glow-discharging.
Glow-discharge the grids for 60 s at 25 mA with negative charge.
Place the microscope slide with grids in a 10 cm glass petri dish and cover against contamination.
Work in a safety cabinet.
Prepare a fresh sterile 1% fibronectin coating solution in PBS.
Place a drop (5–10 μL) of 1% fibronectin coating solution on each grid.
Let the grids dry for 1 hour under UV light inside the safety cabinet.
Apply fibronectin coating solution on glow-discharged holey carbon-coated gold finder grids (Quantifoil R2/1).
Incubate under UV-light for 1 hour.
Wet grids with PBS.
Wash grids in PBS.
Place grids in medium-filled ibidi chamber slide square.
Mix cells and virus at MOI:2 in Eppendorf tube.
Pipette small volume on grid.
Check cell distribution with light microscopy.
Repeat until satisfied with the distribution.
Prepare one ibidi chamber slide by putting 50 μL of GM in each well.
Prevent drying of the sample during incubation.
Place medium in all wells for protection against drying.
Alternatively, place the ibidi chamber slide in a 10 cm cell culture dish with wet lint-free tissue to create a wet chamber.
Wash each grid in PBS to remove excess fibronectin coating solution.
Dip each grid and place one per well in a + pattern inside the ibidi chamber slide squares.
Preheat trypsin, PBS and GM to 37°C.
Remove medium from the cell culture dish.
Wash cells once with 5 mL of PBS.
Give 2 mL of trypsin to the dish and place in incubator for 15–20 min.
Stop trypsinization reaction with 3 mL of GM.
Prepare a counting chamber (Neubauer Improved).
Pipette 10 μL of cell-suspension into the Neubauer Improved counting chamber.
Place remaining cells back in the incubator to keep them warm.
Count all the cells in up to 4 squares under a light microscope.
Calculate the number of cells per mL using counted cells × 10^4 divided by the number of counted squares.
Mix 0.5 ml of cells with virus at an MOI of 2 in a screwcap tube with a rubber seal.
Store virus in small aliquots to avoid loss of infectivity through freeze-thaw cycles.
Optimize the MOI needed to get at least 80% of cells infected.
Seed cells on grids by pipetting 5 μL of cell-suspension over one grid.
Break the surface of the medium while pipetting instead of dropping a drop of cells.
Consider seeding the cells prior to infecting them for short timeframes, and then adding virus above the grid through the surface of the medium.
Check the cellular distribution of the grid with a light microscope.
Repeat step 5a until ideally each grid square in the middle area has on average one cell.
Discard grids with too much broken carbon.
Do not mix different conditions in one chamber to avoid cross-contamination.
Put the ibidi chamber slide into an incubator and let the cells attach.
Take grids out of their box and place them foil-side up onto a microscope slide.
Place the microscope slide into a carbon coater (e.g., Leica ACE600) and apply a 5 nm carbon coat onto the grid.
Glow discharge the grids for 60 s, 25 mA, negative charge.
Submerge the grid foil-side up into the drop of PLL-g-PEG and incubate for 1 h at RT in a wet chamber.
Add 5 μL PLPP (4-benzoylbenzyl-trimethylammonium chloride, 14.5 mg/mL) into the cavities of a glass bottom ibidi μ-Dish 35 mm low with up to 4 PDMS stencils.
Retrieve grids from PLL-g-PEG using a tweezer.
Touch the grid’s backside with a filter paper to dry briefly.
Place the grid into the PLPP drop with the foil-side facing downwards.
Close the ibidi dish lid immediately after placing the grid.
Switch on the microscope including the PRIMO setup.
Put the ibidi dish into the microscope.
Use LEONARDO software to perform photopatterning using the PRIMO system.
Calibrate the system by marking 5 mm on the glass in the same dish if possible.
Follow on-screen instructions for calibration.
Use bright-field illumination to center the grid image.
Adjust focus to the grid foil.
Click on the magic wand icon to open the Experimental Wizard and select TEM Grids.
Select your pattern of interest from the pattern selection panel.
For A549 cells, use a simple triangular shape placed in the center of the grid square.
Set the settings to the values provided in Table 1.
Select an ROI of 500 μm to cover the center of the grid with patterns.
Click on Add Grid to place patterns.
Click on Finish to confirm the placement of your patterns.
Click on Play to start the photopatterning.
Switch off the bright-field illumination during the photopatterning process.
Apply the pattern only in well-focused areas.
Ensure critical focus to achieve sharp and accurate photopatterning results.
Use an image editing software and create a black square (200 px × 200 px).
Place the pattern design in white or greyscales in the center of the black square with dimensions of 100 px × 100 px.
Save the pattern under Program Files -> Micro-Manager-1.4 -> patterns as an 8bit grayscale image in .tif format.
Restart the LEONARDO software if it is already running.
Prepare two Eppendorf tubes containing PBS and a microscope slide with parafilm and a 20 μL drop of PBS for each grid.
Place the ibidi dish with photopatterned grids into the hood.
Carefully remove the PDMS stencil using tweezers.
Pick up each grid individually and immediately dip them into the first PBS tube.
Wash the grid by repeatedly submerging it into the PBS 10–15 times.
Move to the second Eppendorf tube and repeat the washing step.
Place the grid foil-side up onto a microscope slide prepared with parafilm and PBS drops.
Pause point: You can store the functionalized grids in drops of PBS at 4°C using a wet chamber for up to a month.
Prepare a microscope slide with parafilm and place a 10 μL drop of fibronectin coating solution (10 μg/mL) per grid on it.
Take the grids out of the PBS and place them foil-side up into the drop of fibronectin coating solution.
Ensure that the grid sinks to the bottom.
Incubate at least 30 min at room temperature.
Incubate/store the grids in the fibronectin coating solution drop in a wet chamber at 4°C for at least a week.
Take the grids out of the fibronectin coating solution drop using tweezers.
Thoroughly wash the grids by submerging them (10-15 times) in Eppendorf tubes filled with PBS.
Place the grid foil-side up into the medium-filled wells of the ibidi chamber slide.
Submerge the grid carefully if necessary.
Retrieve the grid vertically when picking it up from a drop of liquid.
Blot away excess liquid from the side of the grid using filter paper.
Detach cells from the culture flask using trypsin.
Keep consistent confluence and duration of trypsinization for reproducibility.
Pipette A549 cell suspension through a 40 μm cell strainer into a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Count the cells according to steps 4a–d.
Dilute cells to a concentration of 5 × 10^5 cells/mL in GM.
Apply 5,000 cells (10 μL) per grid for seeding.
Pipette with pipet tip into the medium to ensure even cell distribution on the grid.
Optional: Pipette 10 μL of cells into a well filled with media but without a grid to visualize coverage.
Note: Avoid using less than 10 μL volume to prevent high local concentration of cells.
Dilute cells to achieve a concentration of 1 × 10^5 cells/mL.
Remove media from the grids.
Add 50 μL of cell suspension to each grid.
Allow floating cells to settle onto the grid for 2 min.
Check distribution under light microscope.
If distribution is unsatisfactory, add additional appropriate number of cells.
Gently shake Falcon tube containing cells before pipetting.
Transfer ibidi chamber slide into a 10 cm culture dish and place in incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 20 min.
Retrieve grids using reverse action tweezers.
Wash off cells on the passivated areas by submerging grid in media-filled Eppendorf tube 10-15 times.
Check result under light microscopy.
Perform a risk assessment when handling biologically hazardous materials with sharp tools.
Seed cells on micropatterned grids considering the trade-off between total coverage of patterned areas and having single cells within individual grid squares.
Place the grid into an ibidi chamber slide well filled with GM.
Transfer the ibidi chamber slide into a 10 cm culture dish.
Place the culture dish into an incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Wait at least 2 hours for A549 cells to flatten out and adopt the micropatterned shape.
Check the vitality of cells on the grids over a time course before starting long experiments (>6 h on the grid).
Observe the growth of cells on the grid regularly and decide when to proceed with the experiment based on this observation.
Perform the desired experiment or proceed with plunge freezing if necessary.
Pre-heat microscope climate chamber to 37°C and start the CO2 flow into the chamber.
Load settings from a previous project or create new settings.
Set the microscope mode to single images.
Include one channel for brightfield.
Include one channel for fluorescence.
Give each grid in the first ibidi dish with grids a number.
Select the 5× magnifying air objective lens.
Select the bright-field channel.
Click on Live to get a live view of your sample.
Center the first grid.
Set the z-height.
Change to a 20× magnifying air-objective lens.
Set the exposure-time and laser intensity to a level that is not saturating all the signal but is strong enough to see the signal clearly.
Adjust settings in the Left Panel under the Acquisition tab in Image settings (standard) and illumination settings (Advanced).
Use image Format 2 × 2 binning, Exposure 130 ms, FIM 100%, IL – Fld. 4, Combi illumination IL, and Camera 100% for mCherry signal.
Use image Format 2 × 2 binning, Exposure 95 ms, Intensity 105, Aperture 24, and Camera % 100 for the bright-field channel.
Set up the first position using a 5 × 5 tile.
Switch on Use Focus Map and show the options for Predictive Focus.
Set the mode to 5 Point and click Find Focuses.
Click on Start to record and stitch the tiles-set for the first grid.
Move to the next grid.
Delete the stored position by clicking the Trash Bin icon in the Stage tab of the Acquisition tab.
Start setting up a new grid.
Critical: Fast freeze grids immediately after imaging.
Save the project in the Open Projects tab by activating the main project layer and clicking the floppy-disk icon.
Export images in .tiff format from the TileScan by right-clicking on the last file and selecting Export Image.
Select the folder, image type (tiff), and channels to export.
Activate Scaled Viewer Image and export overlay as scaled Viewer Image.
Click Save for exported files.
Switch off the software and computer according to the local instrument protocol.
Assemble the plunger and take a bottle of fresh and clean LN2.
Cool down the system with LN2.
Avoid spilling LN2 in the ‘cup’ for the propane/ethane 63:37 (v/v).
Wear gloves when working under BSL2 conditions.
Be mindful of burning risks when handling LN2 while wearing gloves.
Do not dip tweezers in LN2 for prolonged periods.
Use dry tissues to absorb LN2 spills by capillary action.
Replace tissues until the 'cup' is completely dry.
Wear a medical mask during steps involving LN2 to prevent ice contamination and allow free breathing.
Cover the chamber with Styrofoam or paper towel to avoid ice contamination.
Wait 10 minutes before proceeding to ensure everything reaches its lowest temperature.
Open the gas bottle valve carefully, ensuring it is just before spilling gas.
Touch the nozzle of the tube connected to the gas bottle to the cold surface of the ethane 'cup'.
Wait a few seconds for the nozzle to cool down completely.
Start a very slow gas flow from the nozzle.
Fill the 'cup' until a convex meniscus is reached.
Mark the Autogrid by placing a red mark across from the milling side on the flat side of the Autogrid.
Mark each side of the wedge at 90° in blue, including the side of the Autogrid for easier orientation.
Place the red mark facing down in the FIB specimen holder and one of the blue dots facing up in the Krios cartridge.
Add a 5 μl droplet of medium on the foil-side of the grid.
Place the tweezers with the grid into the manual plunge freezer.
Blot for 8 s from the back of the grid (where the cells are not sitting) with Whatman No. 1.
Plunge the grids into the liquid ethane/propane.
Place the grid in a grid box precooled in LN2.
Store the grid boxes in a LN2 storage system or proceed directly with clipping.
Thaw the plunger setup.
Disinfect all surfaces that had contact with LN2.
Load c-clips for clipping tools preparation.
Mark FIB-Autogrids with a small dot on the rim in the middle across of the wedge and two dots at 90° and -90° degrees from that dot.
Cool down the clipping station.
Transfer the first batch of grids, as well as the clipping tools into the LN2.
Clip the grids with cells facing down by creating an Autogrid-TEM grid-c-clip sandwich (Autogrid assembly).
Flip the Autogrid assembly in the stations groove to ensure that the clip is attached properly.
Store them in a grid box with the wedge-marking dot (in this case red) facing down.
Cool down the Aquilos 2 loading station with LN2.
Wait for minimal bubbling of the LN2.
Transfer 1 or 2 Autogrid assemblies from the grid storage box to the FIB/SEM shuttle.
Orient the Autogrid assembly with cells facing up and the mark facing towards yourself.
Fix the Autogrid assembly in the shuttle.
Flip the shuttle into loading position carefully and slowly.
Check whether the Autogrid assemblies are secured properly.
Transfer the shuttle from the loading station into the microscope chamber with an evacuated transfer rod.
Inspect both grids with SEM images at the lowest magnification.
Increase magnification to be able to focus the image and link the stage to working distance prior to GIS deposition.
Take tile sets of both grids using MAPS.
Load the fluorescence image of your selected grid into MAPS by right-clicking on a new Layer in the Layer control and selecting Import Images.
Find the image of your grid and open it in MAPS, allowing the program to rescale if necessary.
Align the image using the 3-point method by finding recognizable features in both images and placing points accurately.
Complete the alignment procedure by clicking the tick-button on the bottom after checking and modifying the alignment.
Save suitable lamella sites in MAPS based on fluorescence data.
Prefer single cells for milling since clusters are often too thick to vitrify properly.
Avoid milling closer than 4 grid squares from the edge of a 200-mesh grid.
Apply a layer of platinum with the sputtering system at 1 kV, 30 mA for 10 seconds.
Open AutoTEM and import the project created in MAPS.
Apply a suitable milling protocol template for the cell type.
Monitor a full milling session to adjust currents and times efficiently.
Modify all milling times by changing milling depth and correction factor.
Perform the preparation step in AutoTEM.
Apply an organic platinum layer with the gas injection system (GIS) onto each grid.
Deposite for 17 seconds to establish a stable protective layer of approximately 4 μm.
Run the automated milling procedure without automated thinning, preferring manual thinning.
Navigate to each lamella after auto-milling is complete.
Perform manual thinning/polishing at a current of 30 pA.
Place polish patterns into the voids that are 1 μm narrower than the void.
Only polish the top surface if the frontal GIS coat hangs down and the lamella becomes unstable.
Judge the lamella thickness from an evenly dark gray SEM image without stripes.
Apply a final sputter coat to the sample at 1 kV, 7 mA for 5 seconds.
Prepare the Krios loading station by filling the station with clean LN2 in a suitable work area according to the biosafety guidelines required for the sample.
Transfer sample boxes into the loading station with a pre-cooled tweezer.
Load the lamella sample in the correct orientation into the autoloader: lamellae must be oriented perpendicular to the tilt axis of the stage.
Dock the cassette into the Autoloader.
Safely dispose of the nitrogen from the NanoCab and disinfect it afterward.
Use SerialEM to acquire gridmaps at low magnification (135×) of all samples in the cassette by running the mapgrids script.
Inspect the gridmaps and assess the quality.
Note any light gray areas in the image indicating well-oriented lamellae.
If lamellae are not oriented perpendicular to the tilt axis, reload the grid.
Load the preferred grid and inspect each lamella at medium magnification (3,600×).
Use high defocus settings during inspection.
Create lamella markers in the navigator.
After reloading a grid, realign the gridmap using the SerialEM Navigator option “shift to marker” or “align with rotation.”
Avoid acquiring data on lamellae with cracks, large ice contamination, or reflections from crystalline ice.
Set the eucentric height by the automatic procedure for each lamella.
Update the z-height of each lamella marker in the navigator.
Decide on a magnification and defocus value for data acquisition.
Check the electron dose of your data acquisition settings.
Calculate the exposure time of the tilt images based on the tilt scheme of the tomogram and set it in the camera setup.
Set the frame time to record dose fractionated data with 10 frames per image at 0° tilt.
Tick the option for frame alignment or perform it during post-processing.
Perform a dose calibration in SerialEM.
Target the first spot to acquire a tomogram.
Refine the eucentric height.
Tilt the stage to a relative 0° of the lamella.
Take an image in data acquisition magnification.
Start tilt series acquisition and observe if tracking and focusing works well by paying attention to the focus values in the SerialEM log file.
Unload the sample from the stage and autoloader after all tilt series are acquired.
Discard all LN2 as well as the samples according to the biosafety regulations suitable for the pathogen used.
Clean all material that had contact with the sample according to the biosafety regulations suitable for the pathogen used.
